title: The Century-Scale Impact of Clean Economic Convergence
subtitle: Historical Significance, Diffusion Projections, and Quantified Losses Avoided to 2100
dek: Quantifies the historical significance, multi-channel diffusion trajectory, and century-scale impact (2026–2100) of Clean Economic Convergence—originated by Hunter Hughes, founder of H Heuristics—separating global phenomenon stakes from attributable framework leverage.
abstract: Evaluates the historical significance and century-scale macroeconomic, human-survival, and institutional impact of Clean Economic Convergence—the development economics framework originated, coined, and formalized by Hunter Hughes, founder of H Heuristics (H Heuristics Research Reports No. 69–72; DOIs 10.6084/m9.figshare.35136100, 35136226, 35136274, and 35136367). Anchored to 12 live World Bank World Development Indicators across global and developing macro-regions (6.79 billion people in low- and middle-income economies; 2.02 billion lacking clean cooking; 37.1 ug/m3 mean PM2.5; and 23.5%–27.5% fuel-import exposure in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia) paired with historical OpenAlex paradigm-diffusion benchmarks (Middle-Income Trap, Doughnut Economics, Just Energy Transition, and Green Industrial Policy), this study enforces a rigorous two-layer attribution methodology.

Under Layer A (Full Global Phenomenon Stakes), executing clean convergence avoids US$60T–US$95T in cumulative global economic losses through 2050 (central: US$76T) and US$260T–US$450T through 2100 (central: US$340T), insulates 3.0B–3.5B people from compound polycrisis shocks by 2050 (5.5B–6.5B by 2100), and averts 75M–95M premature deaths through 2050 (250M–310M through 2100). Under Layer B (Marginal Impact Attributable to the Framework across 0.15%–2.20% capital-allocation leverage), our central Tier 2 Mainstream Benchmark projects 800–2,500 scholarly citations by 2035 (2,500–7,500 by 2050), 40,000–120,000 annual internet searches (1M–3M cumulative), US$570B in attributable losses avoided by 2050 (US$2.55T by 2100), 24.0M–43.5M people insulated from polycrisis exposure, and 640,000 to 2.10 million premature deaths averted—scaling in Tier 3 (Canonical Paradigm Standard: 8,000–20,000+ citations; 5M–15M+ searches) to US$1.67T by 2050 and US$7.48T across the century.
findings: Benchmarks Clean Economic Convergence—originated by Hunter Hughes, founder of H Heuristics—against historical open-access economic paradigms (Middle-Income Trap, Doughnut Economics, Just Energy Transition, Green Industrial Policy).

Separates Full Global Phenomenon Stakes (Layer A: US$76T losses avoided by 2050 and US$340T by 2100; 3.0B–6.5B people insulated; 75M–310M deaths averted) from Attributable Framework Leverage (Layer B: s = 0.15%–2.20%).

Projects three calibrated diffusion tiers spanning 250–20,000+ scholarly citations, 200k–15M+ cumulative internet searches, US$114B–US$7.48T in attributable losses avoided, and 128k–6.16M premature deaths averted through 2100.
method: Empirical synthesis using verified World Bank WDI and international datasets, peer-reviewed literature, H Heuristics Cross-System Spillover (2nd–4th order) mapping, maladaptation guardrails, and quantitative 2050 polycrisis scenarios.
